solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Debussy's piece is less convincing

definitions.meaning: ... is Debussy's orchestral work about the sea
lame in the sense of feeble or unpersuasive, here in its comparative form

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a Debussy composition as weaker than the rest of the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Debussy's La Mer, run together, is also the comparative of 'lame', as in a lame excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning feeble or weak, as an excuse can be, and the run-together title of Debussy's sea piece.

clue.text: My, my, the plastic's disrupted biological network!

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at plastic wrecking a natural system.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's lymph vessels and nodes form a network that drains fluid and fights infection.

clue.text: On a dry day no one will want this wine

definitions.text: On a dry day no one will want this wine

parts.words: On a dry day no one will want this wine
parts.note: a raincoat is not worn in fine weather, so nobody wants a ..., and those two words run together name a Burgundy wine

explanation.surface: A wine nobody fancies on a dry day.
explanation.walkthrough: MAC is the British short form of mackintosh, a raincoat; nobody wants a MAC ON when it is dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a red or white Burgundy from the area around the French town of that name.

clue.text: Concerned with matter for discussion being put in print again

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an issue is a topic under debate

explanation.surface: An item about a controversial topic is printed once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To republish a book or stamp is to bring it out again.

clue.text: Angels, heading off to restrict devil, providing introductory thoughts?

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece encloses the other
the first letter of the angels' word is removed, its head taken off

parts.note: seraphs are angels of the highest order
a devil of a job is a pig of a job: something awkward and troublesome

explanation.surface: Some heavenly beings, held back from a devil, offer up opening thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devil' and PIG meet in 'a pig of a job', a devil of a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigraphs are short quotations set at the start of a book or chapter, so they are opening thoughts, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Upset some oversexed old lovers

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters are read backwards
some means part of the word oversexed is used

explanation.surface: Some sex-mad former partners are upset.
explanation.walkthrough: SEXE sits inside 'oversexed'; 'Upset' turns it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Former spouses or partners, from the prefix meaning former.

clue.text: Aggressive or nice, somehow bottling a fury that's silly, about nothing?

indicators.note: bottling means holding inside, so the rearranged nice encloses the rest
somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of nice are rearranged
about means going round, so the jumbled fury encloses the ring
silly means daft, so the letters of fury are rearranged

parts.note: O, the round figure, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Is it aggressive or nice to hold in a pointless rage?
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams nest: 'silly' turns FURY into YURF, which with A goes 'about' the O to make YOURFA; NICE, rearranged as IN..CE, is 'bottling' that.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrase for blatantly confrontational or provocative behaviour.

clue.text: Soldiers needing ceremonial attire correct

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
full dress is formal uniform

explanation.surface: Troops who need formal uniform put things right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correct' looks like an adjective about the uniform, but it is the verb meaning to put right.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy a wrong or set something right.

clue.text: Quiet minister, excellent, went ahead and won the day

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for soft
Rev is the title of a clergyman
A1, first-rate, written as AI
to have led is to have gone in front

explanation.surface: A quiet clergyman of the first rank pushed ahead and triumphed.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, appears as AI with the figure read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To have triumphed or come out on top, an idiom for victory.

clue.text: Marooned son's ill, abandoned individual in a Pacific location

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sick son, stranded and left behind on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like it goes with 'Marooned', but it rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of the Solomon Islands, the Pacific nation east of New Guinea.

clue.text: Plant provided by gardening girl to cover ridged structure

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Mary, Mary, quite contrary, of the nursery rhyme, asks how her garden grows
a chine is a backbone or a ridge of land

explanation.surface: A girl who gardens provides a plant to cover a ridged frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like something growing in Mary's garden, but it means industrial equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant in the industrial sense is the machinery and equipment used in a factory or works.

clue.text: Live broadcast's core element fine

indicators.note: the core of a word is its centre, so the middle letter of the nine-letter broadcast is taken

parts.note: fine and well both mean in good health

explanation.surface: A live broadcast whose central element is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like an adjective about the broadcast, but it is the verb meaning reside.
explanation.definitionFit: To live somewhere is to reside or make one's home there.

clue.text: Just a house — use as place of retreat

parts.note: a nest is a snug refuge or hideaway

explanation.surface: Just a house to use as somewhere to get away from it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely', but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A just person is fair and upright, which is what being truthful and principled amounts to.

clue.text: Half-hearted saint with inadequate bunch of fighters

parts.note: St Luke the evangelist

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an army is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A saint leads a small, unenthusiastic band of fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' trims ARMY to ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm means tepid, and figuratively lacking enthusiasm or conviction.

clue.text: Sight in the heavens turns sailor into ferocious person

indicators.note: turns tells the solver that the answer, obeyed as an instruction, changes the seaman
the result of doubling the seaman's word is tartar, a fierce and violent person

parts.note: a sailor is a tar; the answer read as ... is the instruction that makes the clue

explanation.surface: A sight in the sky turns a seaman into a savage.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as 'double's tar', is an instruction that makes TAR into TARTAR, a fearsome person.
explanation.definitionFit: Two stars close together in the night sky, seen as one point of light.

clue.text: Dumped old females given confidential advice?

parts.note: to tip rubbish is to dump it
F is female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Elderly women thrown out are given some inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tipped off is to receive a private warning or inside information.

clue.text: Tramp again disturbed shoos off a bird

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged once the A has gone

explanation.surface: A vagrant, bothered once more, shoos away a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoos off a' takes one A from the TRAMPAGAIN letters before 'disturbed' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouse of mountain and Arctic regions that turns white in winter.

clue.text: Room for improvement?

parts.note: the phrase usually means scope to do better, but here it is a literal room where one goes to improve one's looks

explanation.surface: The familiar phrase for scope to do better.
explanation.walkthrough: A beauty salon is a room you visit for improvement to your appearance; the salons of old improved the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty or hairdressing parlour is a room where appearance is improved, and a literary gathering improves the mind.

clue.text: Cold, something inclined to give one pain

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a ramp is a sloping surface

explanation.surface: Cold and a slope combine to give someone an ache.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a painful involuntary muscle spasm, a specific kind of pain.

clue.text: Offer from head of state, spending tiny bit of money as before

indicators.note: spending means using up, so this sum leaves the word

parts.note: a president is a head of state

parts.words: tiny bit of money as before
parts.note: one old penny, written 1D in pre-decimal money and read as ID

explanation.surface: A head of state makes an offer while spending only a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: Pre-decimal British money wrote a penny as d, so one penny was 1d; read as letters that is ID.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to offer or hand it over formally.

clue.text: Some maybe in seats support opponents at match

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
the two teams in a match are sides

explanation.surface: Spectators in their seats get behind the rival teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some maybe in seats' looks like a description of fans, but it means what sits on the seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottoms are what people sit on, so they are found in seats, with 'maybe' marking an example.

clue.text: Funny folk, the best sort during extremes of seriousness

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece sits inside the other
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the cream is the pick of the bunch

explanation.surface: Comedians, the finest kind, appear amid serious material.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is informally a hilarious person, so the plural is very funny people.

clue.text: City, finally beaten 'ollow, wailed

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word city
the dropped H of hollow tells the solver to drop the H from the beaten word too

parts.note: hammered means thrashed, beaten hollow

explanation.surface: A city side, thrashed hollow, howled about it.
explanation.walkthrough: To be beaten hollow is to be hammered; written 'ollow, with its H dropped Cockney-style, it tells you to drop the H from HAMMERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to complain loudly or wail on and on.

clue.text: Good old man embracing modern music? That's the spirit!

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man
rap is a modern style of music

explanation.surface: A decent old dad who takes to rap gets an encouraging cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the spirit!' reads as encouragement, but it points to a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape residue, so it is a spirit.

clue.text: Box in church for money

parts.note: to pen is to shut in or confine
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A collection box in church for donations.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennies in plural are coins, small sums of cash.

clue.text: Crowd gathered in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is as it sounds

parts.note: I gather means I hear, so gathered means learned by being told

explanation.surface: A crowd assembled inside a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' looks like the crowd assembling, but it means learned by being told.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of animals, and by extension a mass of people.

clue.text: Language of fierce female putting son off repeatedly

indicators.note: putting off together mean sending away, so letters are removed from the fierce female
off, with putting, signals that something is taken away

parts.note: a tigress is a female tiger, a byword for ferocity

indicators.note: repeatedly means more than once, so the letter for son is taken twice

explanation.surface: A language spoken by a fierce woman who keeps sending her son away.
explanation.walkthrough: S is son; removing it twice takes both S's from TIGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigre is a Semitic tongue spoken in Eritrea and Sudan.

clue.text: Dead, then ending in Elysium? It's different for this lot!

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are rearranged
ending in points to the last letter of the word Elysium

explanation.surface: Once dead, and ending up in Elysium? Not for these people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges DEAD THEN plus M. Elysium is the classical paradise, where the damned do not go.
explanation.definitionFit: The damned are souls condemned to hell, the lot for whom the afterlife is not Elysium.

clue.text: Idiot gets tied up outside and watched

indicators.note: outside means the second piece goes round the first

parts.note: a boat tied up is moored
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool gets tied up outdoors and kept under observation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idiot gets tied up' reads as the fool being bound; the tying belongs to a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor something is to keep it under observation.

clue.text: Cox maybe in vessel that's lost in the morning

indicators.note: losing means a piece is taken away from the vessel's word

parts.note: a steamer is a ship
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A rowing cox aboard a ship that goes missing early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cox' looks like the man in the boat, and so it is: to steer is his job, read as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cox guides a rowing boat, and to guide a boat's course is the verb meant, with 'maybe' marking the example.
